title: WPA band, Gilbert Young and playing on advertising trucks
summary: Listening to his teacher's WPA band and trumpeter Gilbert Young; truck bands, tailgate trombone, Mardi Gras pay of eight dollars.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: To any of the places you remember going? I mean to listen to music? Rather, you know, in the audience rather than as a player?

Yeah, now the WPA band, that's the band they had, where my first teacher was teaching, because when he started directing the WPA band, he had to give up his students. He couldn't have any other job, couldn't have another job working with the WPA band. But he, when he was there with the WPA band, I used to go out in Shakespeare Park. They call it Davis Park now. And I would go out there and hear them play, because there was a trumpet player in that band. I used to admire his tone, his style. A fellow named Gilbert Young, he had a lot of influence over me. His playing influenced me a lot. He had a big pretty tone, a big pretty sound. And there were so many trumpet players that I heard that were playing on the trucks. I didn't get a chance to hear them, just saw them once. Now, they didn't have any sound trucks to go around to advertise. Like if you want to advertise something, you get a band and they get a truck and they play on the truck. Now like that's where this, where tailgate comes from. See like they would put a tailgate down on the truck and have the trombone play out there. See because if you put the trombone play in the back, he'd be jiggled everybody with the slide. Now I used to play on the truck. I used to play on the truck. I used to play on the truck. I was a little boy. And I remember the best jobs musicians could have at that time was doing mardi gras. Yeah, tell me about mardi gras. Now mardi gras. We get a job. All the while we've been playing for a dollar and a half, a dollar. Five dollars at the most. But when you play on mardi gras at the most. But when you play on mardi gras D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G D&G on the truck, you get eight dollars. Guys be looking forward, some guys wouldn't even pick up their hoe until it's time for Mardi Gras, so they can make that eight dollars.
Who'd you work for on Mardi Gras Day?

Oh, that's been so long, I forgot. Different clubs, the clubs, like you have a pleasure club, about 10 people, when you rent a truck, and they have the band on there, on the truck, and they have a lot of whiskey, they have a good time, and with the music on there, they're dancing on the truck.
